meta.title: FEAT-005 · Account hardening
meta.subtitle: Design solution from technical-design.md: lockout, set a first password, gateway rate limits and the sign-in audit log. Pick a flow to follow one use-case path; click any arrow for its data contract.
meta.description: Every sign-in and password request first passes the gateway's rate limiter: 10 per minute per IP for the anonymous /v1/users endpoints and the Google callback, 10 per minute per user for the password endpoints. Identity then checks the account's lockout row: a locked account is answered 423 without checking the password. Each wrong password, and each wrong current password on change password, adds one failure; the fifth within 15 minutes locks the account for 15 minutes. Every sign-in success, failure and lockout is written to audit_entries in the same transaction, without email or IP, and a sweeper deletes rows older than 90 days. A user without a password sets one through PUT /v1/me/password/initial after a Google sign-in in the last 10 minutes; when the sign-in is older, the page sends the user through /bff/login?reauth=true, which asks Identity's authorize endpoint for max_age=60 and so for a fresh Google sign-in. Google sign-in is never blocked by a password lockout.

nodes.label: Browser
nodes.desc: The user. Holds the BFF cookie (gateway) and hs.idp (Identity), which now carries auth_time and amr (pwd or google).

nodes.label: Storefront SPA
nodes.desc: Sign in: 423 shows the locked message, 429 and ?error=common.rate_limited the rate-limit message; an error without returnUrl shows a Try again button. Password page: set mode when hasPassword is false; a 403 offers Continue with Google (/bff/login?reauth=true&returnUrl=/profile/password); 423 and 429 in change mode. Profile card: "Set a password".

nodes.label: Gateway + BFF
nodes.desc: Policy auth: 10/min per client IP on /v1/users* and the Google callback. Policy auth-user: 10/min per sub on /v1/me/password*. Over the limit: 429 common.rate_limited with Retry-After, or a redirect to /signin?error=… for the callback. Client IP from X-Forwarded-For only when Gateway:TrustForwardedFor. /bff/login?reauth=true adds max_age=60.

nodes.label: Identity
nodes.desc: Domain: SignInLockout, LockoutPolicy (5 / 15 min / 15 min), AuditEntry. Application: LockoutRecorder (3 tries on conflict), changed SignInHandler and ChangeMyPasswordHandler, new SetMyPasswordHandler, Google audit rows. Api: PUT /v1/me/password/initial, auth_time/amr in hs.idp and tokens, max_age in /connect/authorize. Infrastructure: AuditRetentionSweeper (90 days).

nodes.label: identitydb
nodes.desc: New sign_in_lockouts (user_id pk, failed_count, window_started_at, locked_until, xmin) and audit_entries (type, method, user_id nullable, reason, correlation_id; no email or IP). Set password inserts a credentials row; OpenIddict rows of other sessions get revoked.

nodes.label: Service Bus
nodes.desc: Outbox relay, at least once. Carries the existing PasswordChanged/v1 after a password is set.

nodes.label: Notification
nodes.desc: Unchanged handling of PasswordChanged (FR-NOTIF-014). FEAT-004's external_login_linked notice gains a link to /profile/password in its password-removed paragraph.

nodes.label: Email provider
nodes.desc: SMTP. Sends the password-changed security email after a password is set.

nodes.label: Google / fake IdP
nodes.desc: FEAT-004's OpenID Connect provider. Used here for the fresh sign-in that set-password requires; a Google sign-in works even while the account is password-locked (D-2).

data.p: Sign-in form, password page (set or change), profile card
data.s: Passwords only in the request body, never stored in the browser

data.p: POST /v1/users/sign-in {email, password} · PUT /v1/me/password {currentPassword, newPassword} · PUT /v1/me/password/initial {newPassword} · GET /bff/login?reauth=true&returnUrl=/profile/password · Google callback
data.s: Responses: 200/204, 401 invalid_credentials, 423 account_locked, 403 reauthentication_required, 409 password_already_set, 429 rate_limited + Retry-After
data.w: Over 10/min: rejected here, Identity not called

data.p: The same requests; bearer token for /v1/me/*; hs.idp passes through
data.s: auth (per IP) or auth-user (per sub) limiter applied first

data.p: Read lockout row; on failure failed_count+1 (lock on the 5th), on success delete it; audit_entries row(s) sign_in_succeeded / sign_in_failed / account_locked
data.s: xmin conflict → reload and reapply, 3 tries; no email or IP stored

data.p: Insert credential (argon2id), revoke other authorizations and tokens, outbox PasswordChanged
data.s: Only when amr=google and auth_time ≤ 10 min; PK conflict → 409 password_already_set

data.p: /connect/authorize?…&max_age=60 → /signin → Sign in with Google (FEAT-004 start, consent, callback, complete) → authorize again
data.s: Fresh auth_time and amr=google land in hs.idp and in the new access token
data.w: Typed password is lost; the user submits again

data.p: FEAT-004 code redeem and ID-token validation (unchanged)
data.s: Google success and failure now write audit rows (method google)

all.title: FEAT-005 design solution
all.intro: Five paths: lockout on sign-in, lockout on change password, setting a first password with re-authentication, the gateway limits, and Google while locked.

steps.t: Sign in with email and password, through the per-IP limiter.
Locked? If locked_until is in the future: audit row, 423 identity.account_locked, the password is not checked.
Wrong password: one more failure and an audit row; the 5th within 15 minutes sets locked_until = now + 15 min and answers 423, the others 401.
Correct password: the lockout row is deleted, sign_in_succeeded is written, hs.idp gets auth_time and amr=pwd.
Locked: 423 before anything is evaluated. Wrong current password: counts on the same lockout (423 when it locks, otherwise the usual 400). Correct: the lockout is cleared.
Set mode (hasPassword false); the first submit gets 403 identity.reauthentication_required because the last Google sign-in is older than 10 minutes.
Continue with Google: /bff/login?reauth=true sends max_age=60; authorize clears the old hs.idp and the user signs in with Google again.
Fresh session: the new access token carries amr=google and a fresh auth_time.
Submit again: one transaction creates the credential, revokes other sessions and queues PasswordChanged; 204 and hs.idp reissued with pwd_at.
11th request in a minute from one IP (register, sign-in, resend, Google callback) or from one user (password endpoints).
429 common.rate_limited with Retry-After, or for the callback a redirect to /signin?error=common.rate_limited. Identity is not called.
Google sign-in (FEAT-004) neither checks nor changes the password lockout.

notes.b: Lockout per account in Identity; request limits per IP or user in the gateway. One guards an account guessed from many IPs, the other many accounts from one IP.

notes.t: Google not blocked by a lockout
notes.b: Otherwise five wrong passwords from anyone lock the owner out completely. Confirmed by the user.

notes.t: Lockout in its own table, xmin
notes.b: credentials.updated_at is the pwd_at stamp and must not move; parallel failures must all count; FEAT-006 locks accounts without a credential.
NFR-LEG-001 limits the personal data we collect; user id and correlation id answer who signed in and when.
auth_time and amr in tokens, OIDC max_age on authorize. A stolen session cannot add a password. Confirmed by the user (OQ-33 proposal).

notes.t: Client IP only behind a trusted proxy
notes.b: X-Forwarded-For is trusted only with Gateway:TrustForwardedFor; the Google callback is limited per IP because no user is known yet.
Registration already reveals that an email exists, so the lock reveals nothing new; 423, not 401, so the password page does not sign the user out. Confirmed by the user.
A newly set password sends the existing security email; no new event contract.
Correct only with one gateway replica (risk R-5). Test stacks raise the limit to 1000 (D-9).
Set password, Google audit rows, the callback limit and the notice link all touch FEAT-004 code. Build and merge it first.
Role-grant audit with FEAT-009; code sign-in lockout and limits with FEAT-006; search and upload limits with their features.
